questions.stem: « En France, le mercredi après-midi, beaucoup d'élèves n'ont pas cours : c'est le moment des activités sportives et culturelles. » What does this show?
options: The school timetable shapes young people's leisure
Wednesday afternoon is a public holiday in France
Students must do homework at home on Wednesdays
Sport is compulsory at school on Wednesday afternoons
questions.explanation: With no lessons on Wednesday afternoon, clubs, music schools and sport fill that time. The text links the school week to leisure habits; it does not describe a public holiday.

questions.stem: « Dans beaucoup de petites villes, les commerces ferment entre midi et deux. » What does « entre midi et deux » mean?
options: between noon and 2 pm
twice a day at noon
from midday until 2 am
two days a week at noon
questions.explanation: « Entre midi et deux » is the everyday phrase for the lunch break, from 12 to 2 pm. Many small shops still close then, a sign of how the midday meal shapes the day.

questions.stem: « Je suis licencié dans un club de foot depuis l'âge de six ans. » What does « licencié » mean here?
options: holding a university degree in sport
licensed to drive a car on the road
registered as a member of a sports club
dismissed from a job by an employer
questions.explanation: In French sport, « une licence » is the membership card that lets you play in a club, so « un licencié » is a registered player. Being dismissed is another meaning of « licencié », but not with « dans un club de foot depuis l'âge de six ans ».

questions.stem: « Elle fait du théâtre dans une association de quartier. » What is « une association » here?
options: a professional theatre with paid actors
a not-for-profit club run by its members
a private company that charges high fees
a government department for the arts
questions.explanation: French leisure life relies on « les associations », non-profit groups run by volunteers for sport, culture or charity. A professional theatre company is not an association de quartier.

questions.stem: « Les Français tiennent à leurs cinq semaines de congés payés. » What does this show about French lifestyles?
options: Paid holidays are valued as a right
French people work only five weeks a year
Holidays in France are usually unpaid
Most French people never take holidays
questions.explanation: Five weeks of paid leave a year is the legal minimum in France, and « tenir à » means to value or be attached to something. The holidays are paid, as « congés payés » says.

questions.stem: « On se fait une petite bouffe ce soir ? » What is being suggested?
options: a quick swim at the pool
a shopping trip in town
a film at the cinema
a casual meal together
questions.explanation: « La bouffe » is slang for food, and « se faire une bouffe » means to get together for a meal. Sharing food is a central French way of socialising.

questions.stem: What does « prendre un café en terrasse » mean?
options: to have a coffee at an outdoor café table
to make coffee on the balcony at home
to buy a takeaway coffee on the way to work
to have coffee on the roof of an office
questions.explanation: « La terrasse » is the outdoor seating of a café, a key part of social life in French towns. People sit and watch the world go by rather than take coffee away.

questions.stem: In spring, Québécois families go « à la cabane à sucre ». What do they do there?
options: go ice fishing on a frozen lake
pick apples in the autumn orchards
ski on the slopes near Québec City
eat a traditional meal with maple syrup
questions.explanation: A sugar shack is where maple sap is boiled into syrup. In spring, the sugaring-off season, families and friends gather there for meals served with maple syrup and maple taffy on snow.

questions.stem: « À Bruxelles, la bande dessinée est partout : sur les murs, dans les librairies et même dans le métro. » What does this suggest?
options: Comics are banned from public places in Brussels
Belgians read nothing else apart from comics
Comics in Belgium are only made for children
Comics are part of everyday Belgian culture
questions.explanation: Comics on walls, in bookshops and in the metro show how present « la BD » is in daily life. « Partout » means everywhere, not exclusively.

questions.stem: Each spring in Paris, what is played at Roland-Garros?
options: the French Open tennis tournament
the final stage of a cycling race
the national rugby championship
a horse race on the Seine banks
questions.explanation: Roland-Garros is the French Open, the Grand Slam tennis tournament played on clay courts, « la terre battue ». The Tour de France finishes in Paris in July.

questions.stem: « En Australie, la vie se passe beaucoup en plein air : barbecue, plage, sport le week-end. » What does « en plein air » mean?
options: outdoors
at full speed
in the fresh morning
in the open sea
questions.explanation: « En plein air » means in the open air. The sentence contrasts an outdoor Australian lifestyle with other ways of spending leisure time.

questions.stem: « Depuis qu'elle a une montre connectée, ma mère compte ses pas tous les jours. » What is « une montre connectée »?
options: an alarm clock
a stopwatch
a smartwatch
a wind-up watch
questions.explanation: « Connecté » describes a device linked to the internet or a phone. Counting steps is a typical smartwatch feature.

questions.stem: « Avec le streaming, on enchaîne les épisodes jusqu'à deux heures du matin. » What habit is described?
options: going to the cinema less and less often
downloading music illegally from the internet
binge-watching series late into the night
watching one episode of a series each week
questions.explanation: « Enchaîner les épisodes » means watching one after another. Québec's official term for binge-watching is « le visionnage en rafale ».

questions.stem: What is « l'e-sport »?
options: competitive video gaming
riding electric scooters
online fitness classes
extreme outdoor sport
questions.explanation: « L'e-sport » (also « le sport électronique ») is organised competition between video game players, often watched by large online audiences.

questions.stem: Which French company created the Assassin's Creed and Rayman video game series?
options: Michelin
Dassault
Decathlon
Ubisoft
questions.explanation: Ubisoft, founded in France, is one of the world's major video game publishers. Michelin makes tyres, Dassault aircraft and Decathlon sells sports equipment.

questions.stem: In April 2023, Parisians voted in a city referendum about which kind of transport?
options: car-free Sundays
shared bicycles
rental electric scooters
the new metro lines
questions.explanation: A large majority voted against « les trottinettes en libre-service », and the rental scooters left Paris streets that September. The vote reflected concerns about safety and cluttered footpaths.

questions.stem: « Grâce à la réalité virtuelle, on peut visiter un musée depuis son canapé. » What is claimed?
options: Museums now refuse visitors who use virtual reality
You can buy sofas in virtual reality museums
Virtual reality has made museums more expensive
Virtual reality lets you visit a museum from home
questions.explanation: « Depuis son canapé » means from your sofa, so the visit happens at home. The claim is that technology widens access to culture.

questions.stem: « Les écrans prennent la place du sport : les jeunes bougent de moins en moins. » What concern is raised?
options: Screens in gyms distract young athletes
Young people move house more often today
Young people are less active because of screens
Sport is now mostly watched on screens
questions.explanation: « Prendre la place de » means to replace, and « bouger » here means to be physically active. The worry is screen time crowding out exercise.

questions.stem: At the opening ceremony of the Paris 2024 Olympics, which Québec singer performed « L'Hymne à l'amour » from the Eiffel Tower?
options: Céline Dion
Isabelle Boulay
Ginette Reno
Diane Dufresne
questions.explanation: Céline Dion sang Édith Piaf's « L'Hymne à l'amour » to close the ceremony, her first big performance after a long break for illness.

questions.stem: What did the swimmer Léon Marchand achieve at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
options: four individual gold medals
a world record in the 50 m freestyle
a gold medal in men's water polo
a silver medal in marathon swimming
questions.explanation: Marchand won the 200 m butterfly, 200 m breaststroke, 200 m and 400 m individual medley, becoming a national hero. He also won a relay bronze.

questions.stem: In 2012, Omar Sy won the César for best actor for which film?
options: Bienvenue chez les Ch'tis
Intouchables
La Haine
Le Fabuleux Destin d'Amélie Poulain
questions.explanation: Omar Sy won for his role as Driss in « Intouchables » (2011), a comedy-drama about a friendship between a wealthy man with quadriplegia and his carer. He later starred in the series « Lupin ».

questions.stem: The singer Stromae, known for « Alors on danse » and « Papaoutai », is from which country?
options: Canada
Belgium
France
Switzerland
questions.explanation: Stromae is Belgian, from Brussels. His songs pair dance music with serious lyrics about family, illness and society.

questions.stem: In the 1998 World Cup final in Paris, what did Zinédine Zidane do?
options: scored two headers as France beat Brazil 3-0
scored the only goal as France beat Italy 1-0
missed a penalty as France lost to Brazil
was sent off as France beat Croatia 2-1
questions.explanation: Zidane headed in two corners in the final at the Stade de France, and Emmanuel Petit added a third. It was France's first World Cup win.

questions.stem: Kylian Mbappé scored a hat-trick in the 2022 World Cup final against Argentina. What was the result for France?
options: They won 3-0
They won in extra time
They lost 1-0
They lost on penalties
questions.explanation: The match ended 3-3 after extra time, with Mbappé scoring all three French goals, and Argentina won the penalty shoot-out. Four years earlier, aged 19, he had won the 2018 World Cup.

questions.stem: Which song is Édith Piaf famous for?
options: « Alors on danse »
« Papaoutai »
« Non, je ne regrette rien »
« Ne me quitte pas »
questions.explanation: Piaf recorded « Non, je ne regrette rien » in 1960; « La Vie en rose » is another of her songs. « Ne me quitte pas » is by the Belgian singer Jacques Brel.

questions.stem: Who created the comic « Astérix » in 1959?
options: Hergé and Edgar P. Jacobs
Auguste and Louis Lumière
Jean de Brunhoff and Laurent de Brunhoff
René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo
questions.explanation: Goscinny wrote and Uderzo drew « Astérix », first published in the magazine Pilote. Hergé was the Belgian creator of Tintin, and the Lumière brothers were film pioneers.

questions.stem: « Elle a décroché la médaille d'or aux Jeux olympiques. » What does « décrocher » mean here?
options: to lose
to drop out
to win
to hang up
questions.explanation: « Décrocher » literally means to unhook, and with a prize or title it means to win or land it. With school it can mean to drop out, which makes no sense with a gold medal.

questions.stem: « Son palmarès est impressionnant. » What is « un palmarès »?
options: a club for the athlete's fans
a record of titles and wins
a programme of daily training
a contract signed with a club
questions.explanation: « Le palmarès » lists an athlete's or artist's wins and awards. It is useful for presenting a prominent person's achievements.

questions.stem: « Elle a marqué toute une génération. » What does it mean?
options: She scored for an entire generation
She marked the exams of a generation
She was born into a famous generation
She left her mark on a whole generation
questions.explanation: « Marquer » means to leave a lasting impression on, and also to score a goal. Here it describes a person's influence.

questions.stem: The comedy « Bienvenue chez les Ch'tis » (2008) plays on clichés about which part of France?
options: the Nord, in the far north
Provence, in the south-east
Brittany, in the west
Alsace, in the east
questions.explanation: A postal manager from the south is sent to Bergues in the Nord and discovers the local dialect, « le ch'ti », and the warmth of its people. The film laughs at regional stereotypes, then overturns them.

questions.stem: The TV series « Dix pour cent » is set in which workplace?
options: a Paris agency that represents actors
a hospital emergency department
a police station in Marseille
a high school in the suburbs
questions.explanation: « Dix pour cent », known in English as « Call My Agent! », follows agents at a Paris talent agency; the title is their commission. Real French film stars play themselves.

questions.stem: The Netflix series « Lupin », starring Omar Sy, is inspired by which character?
options: Fantômas, a masked villain of silent films
Tintin, a young reporter in Belgian comics
Arsène Lupin, a gentleman burglar of early 1900s novels
Maigret, a police inspector in novels set in Paris
questions.explanation: Maurice Leblanc's Arsène Lupin stories began in 1905. In the series, a modern Parisian uses Lupin's methods to avenge his father.

questions.stem: « Cette série cartonne chez les ados. » What does it mean?
options: The series is a big hit with teenagers
The series is being filmed in a school
The series has been cancelled by teens
The series is made of cardboard sets
questions.explanation: « Cartonner » is informal for being a huge success. It is a common verb in reviews of films, series and songs.

questions.stem: In informal French, what does « kiffer » mean?
options: to get bored
to show off
to really like
to make fun of
questions.explanation: « Kiffer », as in « Je kiffe cette chanson », means to love or really like. It is slang, so it suits a text message to a friend but not a formal letter.

questions.stem: « Ce concert était trop ouf ! » « Ouf » is verlan for which word?
options: fort
fun
faux
fou
questions.explanation: Verlan reverses syllables: « fou » becomes « ouf », meaning crazy or amazing here. The slang of young people is part of youth culture in France.

questions.stem: « Le tube de l'été passe en boucle à la radio. » What does « en boucle » mean?
options: in a remixed version
at full volume
on repeat, over and over
very late at night
questions.explanation: « Une boucle » is a loop, so « en boucle » means played again and again. « Le tube de l'été » is the hit song of the summer.

questions.stem: What are « les Victoires de la musique »?
options: a national school singing contest
a radio station for new music
France's annual music awards
a music festival held in Lyon
questions.explanation: Held each year since 1985, « les Victoires de la musique » reward French artists, albums and songs, much as the ARIA Awards do in Australia.

questions.stem: « Les séries françaises s'exportent : de plus en plus de jeunes à l'étranger apprennent le français en les regardant. » What does the writer claim?
options: Young people abroad dislike French series
French series are dubbed into English only
French series spread the language abroad
French series are made for foreign viewers
questions.explanation: « S'exporter » means to be sold and watched abroad, and the second clause says viewers learn French from them. Youth culture is presented as a source of influence beyond France.
